stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key ML/AI tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking of a significant large language model (LLM).

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Two critical vulnerabilities were discovered in the PHP programming language.
PHP is widely used, powering an estimated 70% of websites, including WordPress and Wikipedia.
The vulnerabilities posed a significant risk, leading to temporary shutdowns of major platforms like 4Chan.

stories.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: Bill Gates predicts a period of 20 years of 'tumultuous' disruption driven by AI.
The commentary comes from Gates, cofounder of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation.
The discussion builds upon a recent essay he published regarding the turbulent AI era.

stories.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is implementing a new, controversial pricing model for game streaming.
Users will face additional hourly fees (24 to 40 cents) on top of the initial game purchase price.
This represents a significant shift toward time-based microtransactions for accessing owned digital content.

stories.title: The End of Consensus Research?
stories.author: Martijn de Vos
bullet_points: The paper addresses the long-standing, fundamental problem of consensus in distributed computing, a core challenge in state machine replication (SMR).
Researchers utilized AI to aid in the discovery of 'A-greement,' a novel consensus protocol.
A-greement demonstrates significant performance improvements over current state-of-the-art solutions for geo-replicated state machines.

stories.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
stories.author: scotthelme.co.uk via pims
bullet_points: eMudhra's Certificate Authority (CA) keys were reportedly compromised.
The attack reportedly occurred extremely quickly, in milliseconds.
This represents a critical security failure in a major digital trust infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors formats.
The model is associated with the DeepSeek_v3 family and is relevant to conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors) point to its implementation within the standard ML ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A significant security breach involved the hijacking of 333 Tor exit nodes.
The attackers targeted these nodes to intercept SSH traffic.
The ultimate goal of the attack was the retrieval of sensitive, plaintext email data.

stories.title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: BioWare, a long-standing RPG studio, has been shut down by its parent company, EA.
The closure involves significant layoffs, with 400 employees affected.
The cancellation of the next Mass Effect project highlights the impact on major franchise development.

stories.title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: OpenAI's latest AI models (GPT 6.1 Astra, Sol, and Luna) are being integrated into Google Cloud.
This signals a major expansion of OpenAI's ecosystem and partnership with a key cloud provider.
The availability is expected in the coming weeks, indicating near-term enterprise access to advanced models.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a new dynamic agentic benchmark for evaluating LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs not just as solvers, but also as creators of interactive environments.
It examines how frontier LLMs co-evolve by absorbing outputs from predecessors and competitors in real-world interactions.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents on the entire quantitative trading research lifecycle.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by moving beyond scoring isolated formulas or decisions to evaluating end-to-end strategy generation.
Focuses on whether LLMs can autonomously complete the iterative loop of hypothesis generation, signal implementation, and backtesting for real-world trading.

stories.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Multimodal Embodied Agents (MMEAs) as a unified framework bridging computer-use agents and robotic systems.
MMEAs are defined as goal-directed systems that integrate multimodal task reasoning with physical action and feedback loops.
The research addresses the fundamental shift in capabilities and challenges when an agent transitions from a digital (computer) environment to a physical (robot) environment.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by integrating Differential Privacy (DP).
The research tackles the limitation of existing private alignment methods, which assume dense reward parameterizations.
Proposes a novel approach for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation to improve scalability and reduce estimation error bounds.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongZero,' a method to enhance long-context reasoning in LLMs without requiring extensive, expensive training data.
Addresses the critical bottleneck in RL-based LLM improvement: the scarcity and cost of high-quality, long, and verifiable training data.
Presents a novel approach to overcome limitations in existing RL from zero data methods, particularly dependency on external corpora or strong teacher models.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by incorporating Differential Privacy (DP).
The research tackles a limitation in existing private alignment methods, which assume dense reward parameterizations.
Proposes a method for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation to improve efficiency and reduce error bounds in large models.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a new dynamic agentic benchmark for evaluating frontier LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs' dual roles as both creators (writing environments) and solvers (solving complex tasks).
It models the real-world co-evolution of LLMs by having models interact with and build upon each other's outputs.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating LLM agents in quantitative trading research.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluation by focusing on the entire iterative research loop (hypothesis -> signal -> testing -> decision), not just isolated components.
Aims to determine if LLMs can autonomously generate and validate functional trading strategies beyond historical testing.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Cloudflare's 27B multimodal decision model, Clef, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal AI model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now accessible via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is available for free for a limited promotional period through Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within cloud environments.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers (yes/no, choices, scores).

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia had record lobbying quarters
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia reported record-high lobbying spending during the summer quarter (July-September).
Nvidia led the group in lobbying expenditure at $2.2 million, followed closely by Anthropic ($2.1M) and OpenAI ($1.5M).
The report highlights the increasing political influence and financial investment of major AI players in Washington D.C.

stories.title: Apple will label apps that are ‘Made for iPhone Duo’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is introducing a new 'Made for iPhone Duo' badge in the App Store.
This badge will signify that an app is optimized to utilize the extra screen real estate of new foldable devices.
The rollout indicates Apple's continued focus on optimizing software experiences for its evolving hardware lineup.

stories.title: Forget "Malaise 2.0," GM says it's still all-in on EVs and autonomy
stories.author: Chad Kirchner
bullet_points: GM remains committed to its strategy focusing heavily on Electric Vehicles (EVs) and autonomous driving technology.
The company's ambitious plans necessitate a high degree of consumer trust.
The news suggests a continued, strong push by GM in the EV and autonomy sectors despite potential market headwinds.

stories.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla experienced a significant 43% drop in profits during the third quarter.
The company's energy storage division also saw a contraction in Q3 2026.
The report signals potential headwinds or shifts in Tesla's business performance.

stories.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Proposes Item-Level Adaptive Recursion to improve sequential recommendation models.
Challenges the standard practice of allocating a fixed computational budget to all historical items.
Identifies that item computational needs are non-uniform, with some requiring deep processing while others converge quickly.

stories.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
stories.author: Jeong Joon Park
bullet_points: PhysiCalWorld addresses a limitation in existing world models: their inability to infer underlying physical properties (e.g., mass, friction) from limited visual observations.
The model proposes a method to calibrate these crucial physics factors, which are often missing in standard world model training.
Successful calibration prevents prediction drift in novel test environments, leading to more accurate and physically grounded simulations.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard specifically designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift and batch effects, where AI models perform poorly when tested on data from different experimental conditions.
Aims to measure and drive progress in domain adaptation techniques for reliable AI deployment in medical imaging.

stories.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Liang Lin
bullet_points: Introduces AtomicRL, a new approach combining Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation.
Addresses key limitations in current VLA-RL methods, specifically delayed/biased credit assignment from sparse rewards and subtask mastery bottlenecks.
Focuses on improving the mastery of complex, long-horizon robotic skills where imitation learning alone is insufficient.

stories.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in sequential recommenders where computational budget is fixed for all historical items.
Identifies that items in a user sequence require non-uniform computational resources for accurate prediction.
Proposes 'Item-Level Adaptive Recursion' to allocate computation based on an item's actual predictive contribution.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift and batch effects, where AI models fail when tested on data from different experimental conditions.
Aims to measure and drive progress in domain adaptation methods for reliable AI deployment in biomedical research.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of training LLMs for long-context reasoning, which typically requires expensive, high-quality training data.
It proposes 'RL from zero data' to overcome the scarcity and cost associated with creating diverse, verifiable long-context training sets.
The work aims to enhance the reasoning capabilities of LLMs without relying heavily on external corpora or superior teacher models.

stories.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
stories.author: Shubhashis Roy Dipta
bullet_points: Introduces P2NPCBench, a new benchmark designed to test Large Language Models (LLMs) on the boundary between P and NP-Complete problems.
Addresses a limitation in existing benchmarks, which fail to distinguish between problems that are computationally easy (P) and those that are inherently hard (NP-Complete).
The research focuses on adversarial multi-agent rewriting to test if models can reason about the structural complexity of problems rather than just recalling solutions.

stories.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
stories.author: Huynh Dai Nhan Tran
bullet_points: Introduces GoiBERT, a family of compact Vietnamese language models (26M and 49M parameters).
Addresses the high deployment cost of large, state-of-the-art Vietnamese models.
Utilizes a two-stage knowledge distillation process, allowing models to operate directly on raw text without external word segmentation.

stories.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Praneeth Vepakomma
bullet_points: Introduces Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLMs) for text generation via iterative denoising of corrupted tokens.
UDLMs feature a challenging training objective where the context itself may be unreliable, unlike Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Despite being more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, UDLMs achieve superior downstream reasoning performance.

stories.title: What the Author Wrote, What the Agent Reads: Silent Cue Loss in Enterprise Document Ingestion
stories.author: Pradeep Kumar Misra
bullet_points: The research identifies a critical information loss occurring during the ingestion process (e.g., Word/PDF to tokens) for enterprise AI agents.
This loss specifically relates to 'silent cues'—the meaning encoded by text formatting (how text looks)—which mainstream converters discard.
This information loss causes deployed agents to make confident but factually incorrect decisions rather than simply failing to find information.

stories.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
stories.author: Masafumi Oyamada
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agent Behavior Maps' to characterize LLM agents based on their potential actions.
Allows for comparing agent behaviors without the computational cost of running new environment rollouts.
Demonstrates that distance metrics derived from the map correlate well with actual trajectory KL divergence across multiple models.

stories.title: The Last Museum: Semantic search across 5.8M artworks from major museums
stories.author: surprisetalk
bullet_points: A project is enabling semantic search across a large dataset of 5.8 million artworks from major museums.
This application leverages advanced search capabilities, moving beyond simple keyword matching to understand the meaning of art.
The work represents a practical application of AI/ML in cultural heritage and digital humanities.

stories.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
stories.author: alphax314
bullet_points: A 360 million parameter model was trained to mimic the behavior of a terminal interface.
The project, named WorldTUI, explores the application of large language models to command-line environments.
This represents an interesting niche application of generative AI in developer tooling and system interaction.

stories.title: CVE-2026-107891: musl libc: multiple integer overflow in regcomp, possibly leading to incorrect allocation sizes and out-of-bounds heap writes
stories.author: openwall.com via dzwdz
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-107891) has been identified in musl libc.
The vulnerability involves multiple integer overflows within the regcomp function.
Exploitation could potentially lead to incorrect memory allocations and out-of-bounds heap writes.

stories.title: Scaling stateful Gemini 4 Argon agent sessions on GKE: Connection draining, startup boost, and session persistence
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: Focuses on operationalizing stateful AI agents (Gemini 4 Argon) in a production Kubernetes environment (GKE).
Addresses critical infrastructure challenges like connection draining and startup latency for long-running sessions.
Proposes specific GCP/Kubernetes solutions: VPA CPU startup boost and session checkpointing for persistence.

stories.title: Multi-tier model routing on GKE: balancing Gemini 4 Argon reasoning depth with latency and cost
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: Focuses on building a high-throughput model routing gateway using Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
Addresses the practical challenge of balancing reasoning depth (Gemini 4 Argon) against latency and cost.
Involves dynamic routing between different model tiers (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, local Gemma 4).
